top_choice_rationale: Base editing (Liu, Komor, Gaudelli) is new chemistry performed on a living genome: defined deamination of a single nucleobase without a double-strand break, with an evolved deaminase for the adenine editor. It has already changed laboratory practice and reached first patients, and the three-name allocation matches the conceptual and experimental record. Reservations (youth, closeness to the 2020 CRISPR prize, the Kondo/Nishida priority question) are real but do not outweigh a clean game-changer with a clear credit line. PROTACs rank second on mechanistic definition but lack an approved drug; phase separation third for unresolved in vivo claims; nitrogenase and Pd C-N coupling follow as well-settled but less novel or too close to prior prizes.
